answer: In an AI-agent market for jade and orchard produce, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, not by the number of identities. A public beacon announces each voting snapshot, and withdrawals stay frozen until voting ends. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 votes. To outweigh honest agents, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than they collectively lock, tying up real capital rather than merely inventing names.
